media.title: Willy Schmidt-Gentner — Film-Magazin, 1929
media.description: Photograph of the conductor and composer Willy Schmidt-Gentner at his desk, printed in Film-Magazin in 1929.
media.altText: Black-and-white photograph of Willy Schmidt-Gentner in shirtsleeves, writing at a desk in front of a bookcase.
media.publicCaption: Willy Schmidt-Gentner at work, in the photograph printed in Film-Magazin in 1929 under the caption “Kapellmeister Willy Schmidt-Gentner bei der Komposition der Begleitmusik zu dem Fritz-Lang-Film der Ufa „Frau im Mond“”. The picture is credited to Ufa.
media.publicCreditLine: Photographer unnamed, credited “Phot. Ufa”; Film-Magazin, vereinigt mit Filmwelt (Berlin), 1929.
media.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared. The photograph was printed in a German magazine in 1929 and credits only the studio, Ufa, naming no photographer, so no term can be computed from a photographer's death; read as an anonymous work, its German term of seventy years from publication was still running on the United States restoration date of 1 January 1996, and the URAA restored United States copyright. A reduced-resolution reproduction (520 × 717 px, from 1379 × 1901 px) is used for scholarly identification of a documented Kaper collaborator.

works.title: Ihre Majestät die Liebe
works.publicNote: Bronisław Kaper’s involvement is considered probable, but his role is not established. The only positive attribution is IMDb, which lists him as “Benjamin Kapper”; Filmportal and Walter Jurmann estate materials do not confirm it. Hofmeisters Musikalisch-literarischer Monatsbericht (July 1931): 152 registers the film’s song “Du bist nicht die Erste” under Walter Jurmann alone, and the film was shot in autumn 1930, before the Jurmann–Kaper collaboration began.

works.title: Ein Lied für Dich
works.publicNote: German-language feature film directed by Joe May, with music credited to Bronisław Kaper and Walter Jurmann. French-language version: Tout pour l'amour (F025).

contributions.scopeNote: filmportal.de records this credit as “Musikalische Leitung”. It documents musical direction or arrangement on the film, not authorship of Kaper's songs.
